title: Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha (Mokṣopāya)
attributionNote: Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha (Mokṣopāya), as Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server catalogues it (MOK), on its own shelf.
description: The Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, also called the Mokṣopāya, "the means to liberation", is one of the longest philosophical works in Sanskrit, traditionally ascribed to Vālmīki. In six books (prakaraṇas) the sage Vasiṣṭha teaches the young prince Rāma, who has come home weary of the world. Its subject is the mind and the world it makes; its purpose is liberation while living (jīvanmukti). It teaches almost entirely through long, nested stories, and is broadly Advaitic in outlook, though more imaginative teaching than technical argument. It is for the reader who, like Rāma, has grown dispassionate and asks what is real; its stories are largely self-contained and can be read one at a time. The summary above is the one Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server publishes for the text, and the server's own metadata records it as AI-assisted (claude-opus-5-5); an editor's note for the work itself is still to be written.
historicalContext: Read in the Heritage Scripture Server corpus, which continues the Gita Supersite built at IIT Kanpur: the text, its classical commentaries and the translations the server may serve are held together there.
availabilityNote: The outline is held: 205 chapter(s) and 7847 verse address(es), read from the server's own catalogue. The verses are not stored — the licence forbids bulk harvesting and database reconstruction — and are streamed from the API one verse at a time as the work is read, with the attribution HCAL-1.1 requires and the server's own quota and licence notice.
